Rule 3: A pair agrees when the B amount figure equals the A amount figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, channel CARD entries and lodgement entries.

Rule 7: Entries of A that share a lodgement number appear in B as one line whose reference is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
Rule 8: A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the lodgement is fine.
Rule 9: B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.

(7) B combines the A entries of one load number into one line with that number as note id and their summed weight, sign reversed; their own note id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(8) A combined line that is short by the exact weight of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the load is fine.
(9) Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
(10) A line of B that carries no note id and no load number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.

Rule 9: Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Reconciliation for January 2026. Ledger A is the stock system in which the Welkada store books its movements; ledger B is the receiving log kept at the Fermora depot.

Matching conventions:
Rule 1: An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their movement id values are identical, character for character.
Rule 2: Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
Rule 3: An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of quantity figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for route SAMPLE and for entries with a pallet number.
Rule 4: The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
Rule 5: Two B lines with the same movement id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its quantity multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
Rule 6: Entries of A with route SAMPLE reach B less a retained test sample of 4 units each: the quantity figure on the B line is 4 units smaller in size than the quantity figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other route has a deduction.
Rule 7: Several A entries with the same pallet number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the movement id column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
Rule 8: When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the quantity of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.
Rule 9: The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
Rule 10: B may hold extra lines whose movement id matches nothing in A (no entry, no pallet number); they play no part.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

7. Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.

Entries of A with method WIRE reach B less a transfer charge of 1.20 each: the amount figure on the B line is 1.20 smaller in size than the amount figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. 9. Entries of A that share a payment run number appear in B as one line whose doc number is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the amount of one entry of the payment run, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the payment run reconcile.

state:
The two records below cover September 2025: ledger A, the purchase ledger kept by Fermeth Trading for the supplier Luskuma Components, and ledger B, the supplier statement sent by Luskuma Components.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their doc number values are identical, character for character.
2. All amount figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
3. An entry reconciles when the amount figure on its B line is its own amount figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with method WIRE and entries with a payment run number follow their own rules below.
4. The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
5. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its doc number; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
6. For every A entry whose method is WIRE, B takes a fixed transfer charge of 0.90 per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 0.90, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other method are not reduced.
7. Entries of A that share a payment run number appear in B as one line whose doc number is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
8. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the amount of one entry of the payment run, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the payment run reconcile.
9. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
10. A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

(7) B combines the A entries of one roll-up number into one line with that number as sheet id and their summed hours, sign reversed; their own sheet id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(8) If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the hours of one entry of the roll-up, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the roll-up reconcile.
(9) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(10) Lines of B whose sheet id is neither a sheet id of A nor a roll-up number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

The two records below cover November 2026: ledger A, the stock system of the Hoskik store, and ledger B, the receiving log kept at the Raskand depot.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their movement id values are identical, character for character.

Entries of A with route SAMPLE reach B less a retained test sample of 2 units each: the quantity figure on the B line is 2 units smaller in size than the quantity figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. 9. B combines the A entries of one pallet number into one line with that number as movement id and their summed quantity, sign reversed; their own movement id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.

Period under review: November 2026. Ledger A is the timesheet of the Ulstolm team, and ledger B is the client hours log signed off by Jelvast Trading.

Matching conventions:
(1) Pairing goes by sheet id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same sheet id.
(2) Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
(3) An entry reconciles when the hours figure on its B line is its own hours figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with mode TRAVEL and entries with a roll-up number follow their own rules below.
(4) A B line dated more than 1 day before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 1 day or less is fine.
(5) Two B lines with the same sheet id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its hours multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
(6) For every A entry whose mode is TRAVEL, B takes a fixed travel deduction of 0.50 h per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 0.50 h, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other mode are not reduced.
(7) B combines the A entries of one roll-up number into one line with that number as sheet id and their summed hours, sign reversed; their own sheet id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(8) If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the hours of one entry of the roll-up, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the roll-up reconcile.
(9) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(10) Lines of B whose sheet id is neither a sheet id of A nor a roll-up number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

Period under review: February 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger of Bralansa Instruments for the supplier Coskik Instruments, and ledger B is the supplier statement that Coskik Instruments issued to Bralansa Instruments.

Matching conventions:
(1) Pairing goes by doc number alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same doc number.
(2) B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
(3) A pair agrees when the B amount figure equals the A amount figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, method WIRE entries and payment run entries.

(7) Entries of A that share a payment run number appear in B as one line whose doc number is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
(8) A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the payment run is fine.
(9) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(10) Lines of B whose doc number is neither a doc number of A nor a payment run number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

state:
Reconciliation for September 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger of Prelevi Textiles for the supplier Ulstont Foods; ledger B is the supplier statement that Ulstont Foods issued to Prelevi Textiles.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their doc number values are identical, character for character.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
5. An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
6. A B line dated more than 3 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 3 days or less is fine.
7. Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
8. Entries of A with method WIRE reach B less a transfer charge of 1.20 each: the amount figure on the B line is 1.20 smaller in size than the amount figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other method has a deduction.
9. Entries of A that share a payment run number appear in B as one line whose doc number is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the amount of one entry of the payment run, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the payment run reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

Reconciliation for July 2025. Ledger A is the cash book kept by Coskont Ceramics; ledger B is the bank statement that Dulvansa Cooperative Bank sent to Coskont Ceramics.

How the two ledgers are matched:
Rule 1: Pairing goes by reference alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same reference.
Rule 2: B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
Rule 3: An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for channel CARD and for entries with a lodgement number.

Rule 5: An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its reference; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
Rule 6: A line for an entry with channel CARD is 0.45 smaller in size in B (processing fee; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 0.45 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 0.45. Other channel values carry no deduction.
Rule 7: Several A entries with the same lodgement number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the reference column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
Rule 8: When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.
Rule 9: The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
Rule 10: Lines of B whose reference is neither a reference of A nor a lodgement number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

At most one entry of A fails to reconcile.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Reconciliation for March 2026. Ledger A is the dispatch register of the Ulsture plant; ledger B is the weighbridge record kept by the haulier Dulvela Haulage.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. Pairing goes by note id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same note id.
2. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
3. A line of B that carries no note id and no load number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. B is kept by the other side, so every weight figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
5. A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
6. The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
7. Two B lines with the same note id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its weight multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
8. A line for an entry with packing PALLET is 18.5 kg smaller in size in B (pallet tare; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 18.5 kg in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 18.5 kg. Other packing values carry no deduction.
9. Several A entries with the same load number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the note id column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
10. When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the weight of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. Pairing goes by movement id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same movement id.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. Lines of B whose movement id is neither a movement id of A nor a pallet number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other route has a deduction.
9. Entries of A that share a pallet number appear in B as one line whose movement id is that number and whose quantity figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the quantity of one entry of the pallet, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the pallet reconcile.

(9) Entries of A that share a pallet number appear in B as one line whose movement id is that number and whose quantity figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.

state:
The two records below cover August 2025: ledger A, the dispatch register of the Zelteth plant, and ledger B, the weighbridge record of the haulier Orstada Haulage.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
Rule 1: An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their note id values are identical, character for character.
Rule 2: All weight figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
Rule 3: An entry reconciles when the weight figure on its B line is its own weight figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with packing PALLET and entries with a load number follow their own rules below.
Rule 4: The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
Rule 5: An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its note id; it then reconciles when the two weight figures add up to its weight with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
Rule 6: Entries of A with packing PALLET reach B less a pallet tare of 22.5 kg each: the weight figure on the B line is 22.5 kg smaller in size than the weight figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other packing has a deduction.
Rule 7: Entries of A that share a load number appear in B as one line whose note id is that number and whose weight figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
Rule 8: When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the weight of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.
Rule 9: The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
Rule 10: Lines of B whose note id is neither a note id of A nor a load number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

Rule 1: An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their reference values are identical, character for character.

Rule 7: B combines the A entries of one lodgement number into one line with that number as reference and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own reference values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
Rule 8: When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.
Rule 9: Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
Rule 10: A line of B that carries no reference and no lodgement number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
The two records below cover May 2026: ledger A, the timesheet kept by the Nolvevi team, and ledger B, the client hours log signed off by Welkela Trading.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their sheet id values are identical, character for character.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. A line of B that carries no sheet id and no roll-up number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
5. An entry reconciles when the hours figure on its B line is its own hours figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with mode TRAVEL and entries with a roll-up number follow their own rules below.
6. A B line dated more than 5 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 5 days or less is fine.
7. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its sheet id; it then reconciles when the two hours figures add up to its hours with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
8. For every A entry whose mode is TRAVEL, B takes a fixed travel deduction of 0.50 h per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 0.50 h, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other mode are not reduced.
9. Entries of A that share a roll-up number appear in B as one line whose sheet id is that number and whose hours figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the hours of one entry of the roll-up, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the roll-up reconcile.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Reconciliation for February 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger of Ulstela Ceramics for the supplier Vasmora Foods; ledger B is the supplier statement sent by Vasmora Foods.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. Pairing goes by doc number alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same doc number.
2. The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
3. B may hold extra lines whose doc number matches nothing in A (no entry, no payment run number); they play no part.
4. All amount figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
5. An entry reconciles when the amount figure on its B line is its own amount figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with method WIRE and entries with a payment run number follow their own rules below.
6. The date of a B line may be up to 1 day earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 1 day means the entry does not reconcile.
7. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its doc number; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
8. A line for an entry with method WIRE is 2.50 smaller in size in B (transfer charge; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 2.50 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 2.50. Other method values carry no deduction.
9. B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
10. When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

state:
The two records below cover May 2026: ledger A, the timesheet kept by the Nolvevi team, and ledger B, the client hours log signed off by Welkela Trading.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their sheet id values are identical, character for character.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. A line of B that carries no sheet id and no roll-up number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
5. An entry reconciles when the hours figure on its B line is its own hours figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with mode TRAVEL and entries with a roll-up number follow their own rules below.
6. A B line dated more than 5 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 5 days or less is fine.
7. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its sheet id; it then reconciles when the two hours figures add up to its hours with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
8. For every A entry whose mode is TRAVEL, B takes a fixed travel deduction of 0.50 h per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 0.50 h, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other mode are not reduced.
9. Entries of A that share a roll-up number appear in B as one line whose sheet id is that number and whose hours figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the hours of one entry of the roll-up, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the roll-up reconcile.

At most one entry of A fails to reconcile.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
The two records below cover October 2025: ledger A, the cash book kept by Tarnure Foods, and ledger B, the bank statement issued by Bralivo Cooperative Bank.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. Pairing goes by reference alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same reference.
2. All amount figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
3. An entry reconciles when the amount figure on its B line is its own amount figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with channel CARD and entries with a lodgement number follow their own rules below.
4. A B line dated more than 3 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 3 days or less is fine.
5. B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same reference; together they must give the entry's amount with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
6. A line for an entry with channel CARD is 0.20 smaller in size in B (processing fee; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 0.20 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 0.20. Other channel values carry no deduction.
7. Entries of A that share a lodgement number appear in B as one line whose reference is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
8. A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the lodgement is fine.
9. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
10. B may hold extra lines whose reference matches nothing in A (no entry, no lodgement number); they play no part.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Period under review: March 2025. Ledger A is the timesheet of the Hoskik team, and ledger B is the client hours log signed off by Dulvansa Trading.

Matching conventions:
Rule 1: Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same sheet id.
Rule 2: All hours figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
Rule 3: An entry reconciles when the hours figure on its B line is its own hours figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with mode TRAVEL and entries with a roll-up number follow their own rules below.
Rule 4: The date of a B line may be up to 5 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 5 days means the entry does not reconcile.
Rule 5: Two B lines with the same sheet id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its hours multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
Rule 6: Entries of A with mode TRAVEL reach B less a travel deduction of 0.50 h each: the hours figure on the B line is 0.50 h smaller in size than the hours figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other mode has a deduction.
Rule 7: B combines the A entries of one roll-up number into one line with that number as sheet id and their summed hours, sign reversed; their own sheet id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
Rule 8: If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the hours of one entry of the roll-up, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the roll-up reconcile.
Rule 9: The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
Rule 10: Lines of B whose sheet id is neither a sheet id of A nor a roll-up number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

Period under review: June 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Galtolm Trading for the supplier Yorvevi Foods, and ledger B is the supplier statement that Yorvevi Foods issued to Galtolm Trading.

Matching conventions:
(1) Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same doc number.
(2) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(3) A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
(4) B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
(5) An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
(6) Dates may differ by at most 2 days in either direction; a gap of exactly 2 days is still accepted, a larger one is not.
(7) Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
(8) Entries of A with method WIRE reach B less a transfer charge of 2.50 each: the amount figure on the B line is 2.50 smaller in size than the amount figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other method has a deduction.
(9) B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(10) When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

state:
Period under review: August 2025. Ledger A is the dispatch register kept at the Vasmivo plant, and ledger B is the weighbridge record kept by the haulier Orstivo Haulage.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. Pairing goes by note id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same note id.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. B may hold extra lines whose note id matches nothing in A (no entry, no load number); they play no part.
4. All weight figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
5. A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
6. The date of a B line may be up to 5 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 5 days means the entry does not reconcile.
7. Two B lines with the same note id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its weight multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
8. Entries of A with packing PALLET reach B less a pallet tare of 20.0 kg each: the weight figure on the B line is 20.0 kg smaller in size than the weight figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other packing has a deduction.
9. B combines the A entries of one load number into one line with that number as note id and their summed weight, sign reversed; their own note id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
10. A combined line that is short by the exact weight of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the load is fine.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Period under review: February 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger of Bralansa Instruments for the supplier Coskik Instruments, and ledger B is the supplier statement that Coskik Instruments issued to Bralansa Instruments.

Matching conventions:
(1) Pairing goes by doc number alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same doc number.
(2) B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
(3) A pair agrees when the B amount figure equals the A amount figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, method WIRE entries and payment run entries.
(4) The date of a B line may be up to 1 day earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 1 day means the entry does not reconcile.
(5) B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same doc number; together they must give the entry's amount with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
(6) Entries of A with method WIRE reach B less a transfer charge of 1.20 each: the amount figure on the B line is 1.20 smaller in size than the amount figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other method has a deduction.
(7) Entries of A that share a payment run number appear in B as one line whose doc number is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
(8) A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the payment run is fine.
(9) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(10) Lines of B whose doc number is neither a doc number of A nor a payment run number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

Reconciliation for December 2026. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Dulvont Ceramics for the supplier Raskik Works; ledger B is the supplier statement sent by Raskik Works.

How the two ledgers are matched:
(1) An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their doc number values are identical, character for character.
(2) Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.

(4) Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
(5) An entry reconciles when the amount figure on its B line is its own amount figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with method WIRE and entries with a payment run number follow their own rules below.

(7) Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
(8) For every A entry whose method is WIRE, B takes a fixed transfer charge of 0.50 per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 0.50, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other method are not reduced.
(9) Several A entries with the same payment run number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the doc number column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
(10) When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

state:
Period under review: August 2025. Ledger A is the dispatch register kept at the Vasmivo plant, and ledger B is the weighbridge record kept by the haulier Orstivo Haulage.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. Pairing goes by note id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same note id.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. B may hold extra lines whose note id matches nothing in A (no entry, no load number); they play no part.
4. All weight figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
5. A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
6. The date of a B line may be up to 5 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 5 days means the entry does not reconcile.
7. Two B lines with the same note id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its weight multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
8. Entries of A with packing PALLET reach B less a pallet tare of 20.0 kg each: the weight figure on the B line is 20.0 kg smaller in size than the weight figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other packing has a deduction.
9. B combines the A entries of one load number into one line with that number as note id and their summed weight, sign reversed; their own note id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
10. A combined line that is short by the exact weight of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the load is fine.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

(8) A combined line that is short by the exact weight of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the load is fine.
(9) B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
(10) Lines of B whose note id is neither a note id of A nor a load number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

state:
Period under review: June 2025. Ledger A is the cash book kept by Bralansa Ceramics, and ledger B is the bank statement issued by Bank of Galtand.

How the two ledgers are matched:
Rule 1: An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their reference values are identical, character for character.
Rule 2: B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
Rule 3: B may hold extra lines whose reference matches nothing in A (no entry, no lodgement number); they play no part.
Rule 4: B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
Rule 5: An entry reconciles when the amount figure on its B line is its own amount figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with channel CARD and entries with a lodgement number follow their own rules below.
Rule 6: Dates may differ by at most 5 days in either direction; a gap of exactly 5 days is still accepted, a larger one is not.
Rule 7: B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same reference; together they must give the entry's amount with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
Rule 8: A line for an entry with channel CARD is 0.25 smaller in size in B (processing fee; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 0.25 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 0.25. Other channel values carry no deduction.
Rule 9: B combines the A entries of one lodgement number into one line with that number as reference and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own reference values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
Rule 10: If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the amount of one entry of the lodgement, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the lodgement reconcile.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

Reconciliation for December 2026. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Dulvont Ceramics for the supplier Raskik Works; ledger B is the supplier statement sent by Raskik Works.

How the two ledgers are matched:
(1) An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their doc number values are identical, character for character.
(2) Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
(3) A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
(4) Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
(5) An entry reconciles when the amount figure on its B line is its own amount figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with method WIRE and entries with a payment run number follow their own rules below.
(6) The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
(7) Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
(8) For every A entry whose method is WIRE, B takes a fixed transfer charge of 0.50 per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 0.50, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other method are not reduced.
(9) Several A entries with the same payment run number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the doc number column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
(10) When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

At most one entry of A fails to reconcile.

Period under review: September 2026. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Prelik Works for the supplier Karvik Works, and ledger B is the supplier statement sent by Karvik Works.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
(1) Pairing goes by doc number alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same doc number.
(2) Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
(3) An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
(4) The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
(5) An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its doc number; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
(6) A line for an entry with method WIRE is 1.80 smaller in size in B (transfer charge; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 1.80 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 1.80. Other method values carry no deduction.
(7) B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(8) A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the payment run is fine.
(9) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(10) Lines of B whose doc number is neither a doc number of A nor a payment run number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

9. Entries of A that share a load number appear in B as one line whose note id is that number and whose weight figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Reconciliation for August 2025. Ledger A is the dispatch register kept at the Mernansa plant; ledger B is the weighbridge record of the haulier Luskivo Haulage.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same note id.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. B may hold extra lines whose note id matches nothing in A (no entry, no load number); they play no part.
4. All weight figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
5. An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of weight figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for packing PALLET and for entries with a load number.
6. The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
7. B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same note id; together they must give the entry's weight with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
8. A line for an entry with packing PALLET is 12.5 kg smaller in size in B (pallet tare; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 12.5 kg in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 12.5 kg. Other packing values carry no deduction.
9. Entries of A that share a load number appear in B as one line whose note id is that number and whose weight figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the weight of one entry of the load, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the load reconcile.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

state:
Period under review: March 2025. Ledger A is the timesheet of the Hoskik team, and ledger B is the client hours log signed off by Dulvansa Trading.

Matching conventions:
Rule 1: Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same sheet id.
Rule 2: All hours figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
Rule 3: An entry reconciles when the hours figure on its B line is its own hours figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with mode TRAVEL and entries with a roll-up number follow their own rules below.
Rule 4: The date of a B line may be up to 5 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 5 days means the entry does not reconcile.
Rule 5: Two B lines with the same sheet id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its hours multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
Rule 6: Entries of A with mode TRAVEL reach B less a travel deduction of 0.50 h each: the hours figure on the B line is 0.50 h smaller in size than the hours figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other mode has a deduction.
Rule 7: B combines the A entries of one roll-up number into one line with that number as sheet id and their summed hours, sign reversed; their own sheet id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
Rule 8: If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the hours of one entry of the roll-up, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the roll-up reconcile.
Rule 9: The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
Rule 10: Lines of B whose sheet id is neither a sheet id of A nor a roll-up number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
The two records below cover December 2025: ledger A, the timesheet of the Yorvansa team, and ledger B, the client hours log signed off by Jelvion Components.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
(1) Pairing goes by sheet id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same sheet id.
(2) Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
(3) A pair agrees when the B hours figure equals the A hours figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, mode TRAVEL entries and roll-up entries.
(4) The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
(5) An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its sheet id; it then reconciles when the two hours figures add up to its hours with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
(6) Entries of A with mode TRAVEL reach B less a travel deduction of 0.50 h each: the hours figure on the B line is 0.50 h smaller in size than the hours figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other mode has a deduction.
(7) Entries of A that share a roll-up number appear in B as one line whose sheet id is that number and whose hours figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
(8) When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the hours of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.
(9) B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
(10) B may hold extra lines whose sheet id matches nothing in A (no entry, no roll-up number); they play no part.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

Period under review: September 2026. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Prelik Works for the supplier Karvik Works, and ledger B is the supplier statement sent by Karvik Works.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
(1) Pairing goes by doc number alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same doc number.
(2) Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
(3) An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
(4) The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
(5) An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its doc number; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
(6) A line for an entry with method WIRE is 1.80 smaller in size in B (transfer charge; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 1.80 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 1.80. Other method values carry no deduction.
(7) B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(8) A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the payment run is fine.
(9) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(10) Lines of B whose doc number is neither a doc number of A nor a payment run number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Reconciliation for February 2025. Ledger A is the dispatch register kept at the Vasmast plant; ledger B is the weighbridge record of the haulier Raskansa Haulage.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
Rule 1: Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same note id.
Rule 2: B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
Rule 3: A line of B that carries no note id and no load number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
Rule 4: B is kept by the other side, so every weight figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
Rule 5: A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
Rule 6: A B line dated more than 2 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 2 days or less is fine.
Rule 7: Two B lines with the same note id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its weight multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
Rule 8: For every A entry whose packing is PALLET, B takes a fixed pallet tare of 20.0 kg per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 20.0 kg, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other packing are not reduced.
Rule 9: Entries of A that share a load number appear in B as one line whose note id is that number and whose weight figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
Rule 10: When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the weight of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

Reconciliation for February 2025. Ledger A is the dispatch register kept at the Vasmast plant; ledger B is the weighbridge record of the haulier Raskansa Haulage.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
Rule 1: Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same note id.
Rule 2: B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
Rule 3: A line of B that carries no note id and no load number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
Rule 4: B is kept by the other side, so every weight figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
Rule 5: A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
Rule 6: A B line dated more than 2 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 2 days or less is fine.
Rule 7: Two B lines with the same note id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its weight multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
Rule 8: For every A entry whose packing is PALLET, B takes a fixed pallet tare of 20.0 kg per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 20.0 kg, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other packing are not reduced.
Rule 9: Entries of A that share a load number appear in B as one line whose note id is that number and whose weight figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
Rule 10: When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the weight of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Period under review: June 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Galtolm Trading for the supplier Yorvevi Foods, and ledger B is the supplier statement that Yorvevi Foods issued to Galtolm Trading.

Matching conventions:
(1) Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same doc number.
(2) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(3) A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
(4) B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
(5) An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
(6) Dates may differ by at most 2 days in either direction; a gap of exactly 2 days is still accepted, a larger one is not.
(7) Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
(8) Entries of A with method WIRE reach B less a transfer charge of 2.50 each: the amount figure on the B line is 2.50 smaller in size than the amount figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other method has a deduction.
(9) B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(10) When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

state:
Reconciliation for September 2025. Ledger A is the dispatch register of the Coskand plant; ledger B is the weighbridge record of the haulier Tarnevi Haulage.

Matching conventions:
1. Pairing goes by note id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same note id.
2. B is kept by the other side, so every weight figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
3. A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
4. The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
5. Two B lines with the same note id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its weight multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
6. A line for an entry with packing PALLET is 12.5 kg smaller in size in B (pallet tare; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 12.5 kg in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 12.5 kg. Other packing values carry no deduction.
7. Entries of A that share a load number appear in B as one line whose note id is that number and whose weight figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
8. When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the weight of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.
9. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
10. B may hold extra lines whose note id matches nothing in A (no entry, no load number); they play no part.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Reconciliation for May 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Vasmuma Ceramics for the supplier Raskevi Components; ledger B is the supplier statement that Raskevi Components issued to Vasmuma Ceramics.

Matching conventions:
Rule 1: Pairing goes by doc number alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same doc number.
Rule 2: All amount figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
Rule 3: An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
Rule 4: The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
Rule 5: Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
Rule 6: For every A entry whose method is WIRE, B takes a fixed transfer charge of 1.20 per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 1.20, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other method are not reduced.
Rule 7: B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
Rule 8: A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the payment run is fine.
Rule 9: B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
Rule 10: A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. Pairing goes by note id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same note id.
2. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
3. A line of B that carries no note id and no load number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. B is kept by the other side, so every weight figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
5. A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.

A line for an entry with packing PALLET is 18.5 kg smaller in size in B (pallet tare; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 18.5 kg in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 18.5 kg. 9. Several A entries with the same load number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the note id column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Period under review: May 2026. Ledger A is the cash book kept by Luskont Instruments, and ledger B is the bank statement issued by Yorvast Cooperative Bank.

Matching conventions:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their reference values are identical, character for character.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. A line of B that carries no reference and no lodgement number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
5. A pair agrees when the B amount figure equals the A amount figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, channel CARD entries and lodgement entries.
6. The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
7. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its reference; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
8. For every A entry whose channel is CARD, B takes a fixed processing fee of 0.45 per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 0.45, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other channel are not reduced.
9. B combines the A entries of one lodgement number into one line with that number as reference and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own reference values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the amount of one entry of the lodgement, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the lodgement reconcile.

At most one entry of A fails to reconcile.

(1) An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their movement id values are identical, character for character.
(2) All quantity figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.

(9) Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.

Reconciliation for January 2025. Ledger A is the stock system in which the Hoskolm store books its movements; ledger B is the receiving log of the Coskast depot.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their movement id values are identical, character for character.
2. Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
3. An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of quantity figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for route SAMPLE and for entries with a pallet number.

6. Entries of A with route SAMPLE reach B less a retained test sample of 1 units each: the quantity figure on the B line is 1 units smaller in size than the quantity figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. 7. B combines the A entries of one pallet number into one line with that number as movement id and their summed quantity, sign reversed; their own movement id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
8. A combined line that is short by the exact quantity of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the pallet is fine.
9. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
10. Lines of B whose movement id is neither a movement id of A nor a pallet number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Period under review: November 2025. Ledger A is the dispatch register kept at the Bralolm plant, and ledger B is the weighbridge record kept by the haulier Yorveth Transport.

How the two ledgers are matched:
(1) Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same note id.
(2) Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
(3) B may hold extra lines whose note id matches nothing in A (no entry, no load number); they play no part.
(4) All weight figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
(5) A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
(6) A B line dated more than 5 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 5 days or less is fine.
(7) B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same note id; together they must give the entry's weight with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
(8) A line for an entry with packing PALLET is 20.0 kg smaller in size in B (pallet tare; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 20.0 kg in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 20.0 kg. Other packing values carry no deduction.
(9) Entries of A that share a load number appear in B as one line whose note id is that number and whose weight figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
(10) If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the weight of one entry of the load, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the load reconcile.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

state:
Reconciliation for May 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Vasmuma Ceramics for the supplier Raskevi Components; ledger B is the supplier statement that Raskevi Components issued to Vasmuma Ceramics.

Matching conventions:
Rule 1: Pairing goes by doc number alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same doc number.
Rule 2: All amount figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
Rule 3: An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.

Rule 5: Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
Rule 6: For every A entry whose method is WIRE, B takes a fixed transfer charge of 1.20 per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 1.20, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other method are not reduced.
Rule 7: B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
Rule 8: A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the payment run is fine.
Rule 9: B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
Rule 10: A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

state:

How the two ledgers are matched:
(1) An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their doc number values are identical, character for character.

(9) Several A entries with the same payment run number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the doc number column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
(10) When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

criteria.none: None: every entry of ledger A reconciles

state:
Period under review: April 2025. Ledger A is the cash book kept by Tarneth Trading, and ledger B is the bank statement issued by Bank of Dulvast.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their reference values are identical, character for character.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. A line of B that carries no reference and no lodgement number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
5. An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for channel CARD and for entries with a lodgement number.
6. Dates may differ by at most 5 days in either direction; a gap of exactly 5 days is still accepted, a larger one is not.
7. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its reference; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
8. A line for an entry with channel CARD is 0.35 smaller in size in B (processing fee; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 0.35 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 0.35. Other channel values carry no deduction.
9. Several A entries with the same lodgement number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the reference column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
10. A combined line that is short by the exact amount of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the lodgement is fine.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

Rule 3: A pair agrees when the B hours figure equals the A hours figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, mode TRAVEL entries and roll-up entries.
Rule 4: Dates may differ by at most 2 days in either direction; a gap of exactly 2 days is still accepted, a larger one is not.
Rule 5: B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same sheet id; together they must give the entry's hours with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
Rule 6: A line for an entry with mode TRAVEL is 0.75 h smaller in size in B (travel deduction; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 0.75 h in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 0.75 h. Other mode values carry no deduction.
Rule 7: B combines the A entries of one roll-up number into one line with that number as sheet id and their summed hours, sign reversed; their own sheet id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
Rule 8: If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the hours of one entry of the roll-up, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the roll-up reconcile.
Rule 9: Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
Rule 10: Lines of B whose sheet id is neither a sheet id of A nor a roll-up number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.
